content.title: The God Delusion debate
content.setting: University of Alabama at Birmingham · 3 October 2007
content.description: Read and watch two Oxford colleagues examine science, faith, morality and the claims of Christianity.

claim.text: Dawkins and Lennox dispute whether scientific explanation supports atheism, whether faith can be evidence-based, and how morality and the claims about Jesus bear on Christian belief.

content.hinge: Does explaining a natural process settle whether that process has an ultimate purpose or source?
prompts: Distinguish a scientific explanation from a philosophical conclusion.
State each speaker’s definition of faith before comparing them.
Separate arguments for God from specifically Christian claims.
content.transcriptCoverage: Speaker-attributed transcript arranged around six theses and concluding statements. Published as a full transcript; not independently aligned word for word with the recording.

reviews.scope: Transcript source, event identity, editorial summary, coverage notes and YouTube metadata review
reviews.note: Checked linked transcript structures and publisher notices; compared participant/event descriptions with the recording listings. Verified YouTube metadata and runtimes on 2026-10-11; rejected a 9:12 Concept of God excerpt and selected the 1:31:47 debate. Summaries are editorial paraphrases. Full recordings were not watched or heard, and word-for-word alignment and whole-event completeness remain unverified. No external transcript body is republished. Existing doctrinal policy is unchanged.
